events.content: Arm Holdings Q3 FY2026 royalty and licensing revenue Neoverse data-center

Arm Holdings’ Q3 FY2026 covered the quarter ended December 31, 2025, and total revenue was a record $1.242 billion, up 26% year over year. [[1]]

- **Royalty revenue:** **$737 million**, up **27%** from $580 million in Q3 FY2025. Arm attributed the increase to adoption of higher-royalty technologies—including Armv9 and Arm Compute Subsystems (CSS)—and increased use of Arm-based chips in data centers. [[1]]
- **License and other revenue:** **$505 million**, up **25%** from $403 million a year earlier, reflecting high-value licenses for next-generation Arm technologies; licensing revenue can also fluctuate with contract timing. [[1]]
- **Neoverse/data-center indicators:** Arm stated that Neoverse CPUs had exceeded **1 billion deployed cores** and that its share among top hyperscalers was expected to approach **50%**. [[2]]
- **Illustrative adoption:** AWS introduced fifth-generation Graviton using **Neoverse CSS V3** with **192 cores**, double Graviton4’s core count. [[2]] 

The key investment takeaway is that Q3 royalty growth was not solely shipment-volume-led: Arm specifically linked the 27% increase to a richer product mix and higher royalty per chip from Armv9/CSS, alongside expanding data-center deployment. [[1]]

Sources:
[S1.1] Exhibit 99.2 FYE26 Q3 (31-Dec-25) Shareholder Letter — https://investors.arm.com/static-files/759b8233-bfab-4d24-822c-b517e447e809
[S1.2] Arm delivers fourth consecutive billion-dollar revenue quarter, extending record-breaking momentum - Arm Newsroom — https://newsroom.arm.com/news/arm-q3-fye26-results

source_references.title: Arm delivers fourth consecutive billion-dollar revenue quarter, extending record-breaking momentum - Arm Newsroom

tool_arguments.query: Arm Holdings Q4 FY2026 royalty and licensing revenue Neoverse data-center results

events.content: Arm Holdings Q4 FY2026 royalty and licensing revenue Neoverse data-center results

Arm’s Q4 FY2026 (quarter ended March 31, 2026) revenue was a record **$1.490 billion**, up **20% year over year**. [[1]]

- **Royalty revenue:** **$671 million**, up **11% YoY** from $607 million, representing roughly **45%** of quarterly revenue. [[1]]
- **License and other revenue:** **$819 million**, up **29% YoY** from $634 million, or roughly **55%** of revenue. [[1]]
- The royalty increase reflected higher royalty rates from broader adoption of **Armv9** and **Arm Compute Subsystems (CSS)**, plus greater deployment of Arm-based chips in data centers. [[1]]
- The licensing result benefited from continued demand for Arm IP, the timing and size of several high-value licensing agreements, and backlog contributions. [[1]]

**Neoverse / data-center read-through:** management said the largest contributor to Q4 royalty growth was **cloud AI**, and that **data-center royalty revenue more than doubled YoY**. [[2]] Management specifically stated that royalties tied to chips built on **Neoverse** had doubled YoY and expected them to double again in FY2027. [[2]] Arm also introduced its **Arm AGI CPU**, its first Arm-designed chip for cloud and AI data centers, during the quarter. [[1]] 

The key investor takeaway is that Q4’s royalty growth rate of 11% understated the strategic strength in data center: the rapidly growing Neoverse/cloud-AI royalty stream was offset within the aggregate royalty line by Arm’s broader and more mature end markets, while licensing grew 29% on large-contract activity. [[2]] [[1]]

Sources:
[S2.1] UNITED STATES SECURITIES AND EXCHANGE COMMISSION Washington, D.C. 20549 — https://investors.arm.com/static-files/adf3bac7-1e91-442e-92e0-5f2d8f1b6a14
[S2.2] Corrected Transcript 1-877-FACTSET www.callstreet.com Total Pages: 15 — https://investors.arm.com/static-files/78526857-5997-46eb-9b65-0d3249d83711
